solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: One leaving tutors takes girl round a former African province

indicators.note: a thing leaving a word is dropped out of it, so the one is removed from the tutors
round means encircling, so the girl's name wraps about the next piece

blocks.note: Roman numeral for one, the letter that leaves

explanation.surface: A girl's tutors depart while she tours a historic region of southern Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: The Vaal is the river that gave the Transvaal its name, meaning 'across the Vaal'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Transvaal was a province of South Africa until 1994, when it was split up.

clue.text: A repeated phrase in Eliot initially identifying taxes

indicators.note: one piece sits in the other, so the poet's letters are placed around the phrase

blocks.note: a riff is a short repeated musical phrase
the poet T. S. Eliot's initials

explanation.surface: A critic spots a refrain that recurs in Eliot's poetry and finds it is about taxation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eliot initially' means Eliot's initials, T and S, which go on either side of A RIFF.
explanation.definitionFit: Tariffs are duties or taxes levied on imported goods.

clue.text: Small island rowing crew talked of

indicators.note: something talked of is heard rather than seen, so we want a word sounding like the crew

blocks.note: a rowing eight is a crew of eight oarsmen

explanation.surface: A boat crew mentions a little island in the river.
explanation.walkthrough: An ait (or eyot) is a small river island, especially on the Thames, where rowing eights train.
explanation.definitionFit: Ait is a dialect word for a small island in a river.

clue.text: In the main, it's a source of upheaval

definitions.text: In the main, it's a source of upheaval

blocks.clueFragment: In the main, it's a source of upheaval
blocks.note: surface reading: in general, something that causes disruption
setter's reading: the main is the sea, and the upheaval is a shaking of the seabed

explanation.walkthrough: 'In the main' looks like 'mostly' but is the poetic 'the main' meaning the open ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an earthquake whose epicentre lies under the ocean floor, a literal upheaval beneath the water.

clue.text: Female flautist's second record

indicators.note: second points to the letter in position two of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A woman flute player makes her second recording.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Record' looks like a music recording, but the answer is a historical record, usually used in the plural.
explanation.definitionFit: An annal is a record of the events of one year, as in a chronicle.

clue.text: Drawn to suits, soldier in written works promises to pay

indicators.note: in places the soldier inside the run of letters made by the other pieces

blocks.note: IOUs are written promises to repay

explanation.surface: A soldier among books of IOUs seems keen on clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: The soldier lands after the first I of the promises, not at a word boundary. 'Suits' looks like clothing but means lawsuits.
explanation.definitionFit: A litigious person is fond of going to law, always ready to bring lawsuits.

clue.text: Of good taste, and reputed to have soft heart

indicators.note: to have something at your centre is to hold it inside you
the heart is the middle, so the soft piece goes in the centre of the other word

blocks.note: what is said to be so is reputed
p is piano, the musical marking for soft

explanation.surface: Someone tasteful is also said to be kind-hearted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Of good taste' suggests refinement, but the answer means flavoursome.
explanation.definitionFit: Sapid means having flavour, pleasant to the palate; the opposite of insipid.

clue.text: Home Counties woman, one married in Barcelona, say?

blocks.note: the Home Counties surround London in the south-east of England

explanation.surface: A woman from the commuter belt round London marries in Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: The Home Counties are the counties around London, abbreviated SE for south-east. 'Say' marks Barcelona as just one example of a Spanish-speaking place.
explanation.definitionFit: Señora is the Spanish title for a married woman, the equivalent of Mrs.

clue.text: Post spy outside English royal house

indicators.note: the spy goes outside, wrapping round the abbreviation for English

blocks.note: to post someone somewhere is to plant them

explanation.surface: A secret agent is stationed beyond the English royal family.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Post' looks like mail but is the verb: to station someone, as a spy is planted.
explanation.definitionFit: The Plantagenets were the dynasty that ruled England from Henry II to Richard III.

clue.text: Fantasist of dismal aspect touring Maine

indicators.note: touring means travelling round, so the dismal word goes around the state

blocks.note: drear is a poetic form of dreary
the US postal abbreviation for Maine

explanation.surface: A gloomy daydreamer travels round the state of Maine.
explanation.definitionFit: A dreamer is someone who indulges in fantasy rather than practical thought.

clue.text: Coach further, and keep, outside right

indicators.note: keep sits outside, enclosing the letter for right

explanation.surface: A manager gives extra coaching and holds on to a right-winger.
explanation.definitionFit: To retrain someone is to train or teach them again, giving further instruction.

clue.text: Character transfixed by horse's carrying capacity

indicators.note: to be transfixed is to be pierced right through, so the horse is driven into the character

blocks.note: tone is character, as in the tone of a place
a nag is an old horse

explanation.surface: Someone is spellbound by how much a horse can carry.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonnage is the cargo-carrying capacity of a ship, measured in tons.

clue.text: Shawl originally for independent care home's use

indicators.note: originally means at the origin, so each following word gives its opening letter

blocks.note: first letters of the five words

explanation.surface: A shawl was first meant for residents of a private care home.
explanation.definitionFit: A fichu is a small triangular shawl worn round the neck and shoulders.

clue.text: Alluring companion exciting Mairi's cat

indicators.note: exciting means stirring up, so these letters are agitated into a new order

blocks.note: Companion of Honour, a British order

explanation.surface: A Scotswoman's cat proves an attractive companion.
explanation.walkthrough: Mairi is a Scottish girl's name. CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British award.
explanation.definitionFit: Charismatic means having magnetic personal charm that draws others in.

clue.text: Napier's function, to record a beat, do we hear?

indicators.note: asking whether we hear it signals a sound-alike of the phrase before it

explanation.surface: A mathematician wonders whether he hears a beat being recorded.
explanation.walkthrough: John Napier, a Scottish mathematician, invented logarithms in 1614.
explanation.definitionFit: A logarithm is the power to which a base must be raised to give a number, the function Napier devised.

clue.text: Dollar cakes with room for moving around

indicators.note: moving things around changes their positions, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A baker pays a dollar for cakes and space to move them about.
explanation.definitionFit: Smackeroo is jocular American slang for a dollar.

clue.text: Practical about boxer given something to chase endlessly

indicators.note: endlessly means without its end, so the final letter is cut off

blocks.note: a stick thrown for a dog to chase

explanation.surface: A sensible boxer is handed something to run after, over and over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endlessly' suggests repeated chasing, but it trims the K from STICK.
explanation.definitionFit: Realistic means sensible and practical, facing things as they are.

clue.text: Gelatinous substance from a river crossing Georgia

indicators.note: the outer pieces cross over the state, holding it between them

explanation.surface: A jelly-like stuff is extracted from a river that flows across Georgia.
explanation.definitionFit: Agar is a jelly made from seaweed, used in cooking and for growing bacteria.

clue.text: Beginning of work involving Italian singer

indicators.note: to involve is to wrap up within, so the opening holds the Italian

blocks.note: bar one, the first bar of a piece of music

explanation.surface: An Italian vocalist starts on a piece of work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beginning of work' looks like a first-letter indicator for W; it is the phrase BAR ONE, the opening bar of a musical work.
explanation.definitionFit: A baritone is a male singer with a voice between tenor and bass.

clue.text: Sound demeanour for one who'll succeed

indicators.note: sound tells us the word is heard, so we need one pronounced like the demeanour

blocks.note: an air is a manner or demeanour

explanation.surface: A sensible bearing is fitting for someone bound to do well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' looks like an adjective meaning sensible; 'succeed' here means take over a title, not do well.
explanation.definitionFit: An heir is the person who will inherit and succeed to a title or estate.

clue.text: Break cover, initially appearing in sloop-rigged vessel

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the opening letter of the next word counts
in places those pieces inside the name of the vessel

blocks.note: a hoy was a small sloop-rigged coasting boat

explanation.surface: A sailor bursts out of hiding and turns up aboard a small sailing boat.
explanation.walkthrough: A hoy is an old single-masted coasting boat, a word met mostly in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: A holiday is a break from work, a period of rest.

clue.text: A second-rate dyer, one avoiding the hard stuff

explanation.surface: A poor-quality dyer turns out to be teetotal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The hard stuff' is strong drink, spirits in particular.
explanation.definitionFit: An abstainer refrains from alcohol, a teetotaller.

clue.text: Pause telepathic communication during ceremony

indicators.note: during means within the time of, so the communication sits inside the ceremony

explanation.surface: Mind-reading takes place in the middle of a ritual, which is halted.
explanation.definitionFit: A respite is a short break or interval of relief from something.

clue.text: Safety device choosy users primarily promote

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so the opening letters of the two words are taken

blocks.note: first letters of choosy and users
to tout is to promote or push

explanation.surface: Picky customers mainly push for a safety mechanism.
explanation.definitionFit: A cut-out is a device that breaks a circuit automatically to prevent overload.

clue.text: Row about this writer's old American car

indicators.note: about means around, so the row is wrapped around everything that follows

blocks.note: this writer is the setter, so this writer's is I'm, short for I am

explanation.surface: A setter quarrels over their vintage American automobile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' rhymes with cow here, a quarrel, but the line meaning gives the letters. 'This writer's' is the setter speaking: I'M.
explanation.definitionFit: A limousine is a large luxurious car, often chauffeur-driven.

clue.text: Mercian king hiding in walled garden

indicators.note: something hiding in the phrase is tucked across its words

blocks.note: across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: An Anglo-Saxon monarch lies low inside an enclosed garden.
explanation.walkthrough: Mercia was an Anglo-Saxon kingdom of central England.
explanation.definitionFit: Edgar the Peaceful was king of Mercia before ruling all England in the tenth century.

clue.text: Stress shown by Conservative wearing new suit

indicators.note: new signals the letters are made into a fresh arrangement
the Conservative is wearing the outfit, so it goes inside it

explanation.surface: A Tory politician shows strain in a new suit.
explanation.definitionFit: An ictus is the rhythmic stress or accent on a syllable in verse.

clue.text: Largely superfluous note about Motown

indicators.note: largely means for the most part, so the word loses its last letter
about means turned round, so the note is read back to front

blocks.note: de trop, French for too much, is used in English for unwanted
the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A mostly unnecessary memo concerns the record label.
explanation.walkthrough: Motown looks like the record label, but it is the city's nickname (Motor Town).
explanation.definitionFit: Motown is a nickname for Detroit, the home of the American car industry.

clue.text: End of shocking scam over Greek character's dumplings

indicators.note: end of points to the final letter of the word that follows
over means turned over, so the scam is read backwards

blocks.note: the 22nd letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A shocking fraud about a Greek's pasta dish.
explanation.definitionFit: Gnocchi are small Italian dumplings made from potato or semolina.

clue.text: Pass school regularly

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is taken

explanation.surface: Someone passes the school on a regular basis.
explanation.definitionFit: A col is a mountain pass, the lowest point of a ridge between peaks.

clue.text: Ultimately unfriendly deed, pinching hotel vessel

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the last letter of the next word counts
pinching means grabbing and holding, so the deed holds the hotel inside

blocks.note: H for hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A hostile act turns out to be stealing from a hotel.
explanation.definitionFit: A yacht is a sailing or motor vessel used for pleasure or racing.

clue.text: My man, the French tragic dramatist

blocks.note: cor, like my, is an exclamation of surprise

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims that their man is the French playwright.
explanation.walkthrough: 'My man' reads as a form of address; 'My' is an exclamation, like the British 'Cor!'.
explanation.definitionFit: Pierre Corneille was a seventeenth-century French writer of tragedies such as Le Cid.
